top_story: After months of confrontation that peaked in March with US threats against Iran’s power grid and Tehran’s warnings of regional escalation, Washington and Tehran have shifted to de-escalation, with the US suspending oil sanctions and Iran agreeing by 22 June to restore UN nuclear inspections and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. That turn lowers the immediate risk of a wider Gulf crisis and offers limited economic relief, but it does not ease the region’s most acute human emergency in Gaza. On 20 June, an Israeli strike in central Gaza killed Al Jazeera cameraman Ahmed Samir Wishah less than two months after his brother, also a journalist, was killed in a double-tap strike, reinforcing the sustained attrition of media workers and the narrowing space for civilian documentation of the war. The regional picture is therefore one of selective stabilization: interstate pressure around Iran has eased, while the violence shaping daily life in Gaza remains entrenched and lethal.
